title: Geometric semisimplicity of simple source Weil sheaves
statement: Let $k_0$ be a finite field, $\ell$ an invertible prime, and $X/k_0$ a scheme whose geometric fiber is irreducible. Every irreducible lisse source Weil sheaf $V$ [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex, def-pod-lisse-l-adic-sheaves] admits an isomorphism $\bar V\simeq\bigoplus_{i<n}T_i$ for some finite family of irreducible geometric local systems $T_i$.

proof.text: Use the proved geometric-socle surjection to present the geometric sheaf as a lisse quotient H of a finite sum of simple geometric local systems.

source.place: Paragraphs 1--3 and 7: geometric constituents, two-point curve restriction and local Frobenius powers; geometric socle/Frobenius orbit step in sk-i-dl-general-real.

proof.text: Prove by induction on the number of source summands that such a quotient is a sum of simple local systems. For zero summands the quotient is zero. Otherwise let I be the image of all but the last summand and Q its cokernel in H. These are lisse; the last simple summand maps epimorphically to Q. If its map is zero then I equals H, and the induction hypothesis concludes. Otherwise simplicity makes its kernel zero, so the map is an isomorphism. Its inverse gives a section of H to Q, splitting H as I plus Q. Apply the induction hypothesis to I and reindex the finite sum.

theorem exists_geometric_semisimple_decomposition
    {k : Type u} [Field k] [Finite k] {l : ℕ} [Fact l.Prime]
    [Fact (ringChar k ≠ l)] {X : Scheme.{u}}
    [X.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))]
    [IrreducibleSpace (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k)).geometricFiber]
    (V : WeilSheaf k l X) (hV : V.IsIrreducibleLisse) :
    ∃ (n : ℕ) (T : Fin n → AdicSheaf l (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k)).geometricFiber),
      (∀ i, IsIrreducibleAdicLocalSystem (T i)) ∧ Nonempty (V.obj.carrier ≅ ⨁ T)
